messages.content: Calculate the slope gradient in degree between two points on a landscape with coordinates (40.7128, -74.0060) and (34.0522, -118.2437).

function.name: calculate_slope_gradient
function.description: Calculate the slope gradient between two geographical coordinates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

point1.description: The geographic coordinates for the first point [Latitude, Longitude].

point2.description: The geographic coordinates for the second point [Latitude, Longitude].

unit.description: The unit for the slope gradient. Default is 'degree'.

message.content:
I’m happy to help you work out the slope gradient, but I’ll need one more piece of information: the **elevation** (height above sea level) at each of the two points.  

The slope gradient (in degrees, percent, or ratio) is calculated from the vertical change (Δ elevation) divided by the horizontal distance between the points:

\[
\text{slope (in degrees)} = \arctan\!\left(\frac{\Delta \text{elevation}}{\text{horizontal distance}}\right)
\]

Without the elevation values, we can’t determine Δ elevation, so the slope can’t be computed.  

If you can provide the elevations for:

* Point 1: (40.7128 ° N, –74.0060 ° W)  
* Point 2: (34.0522 ° N, –118.2437 ° W)

— or if you have a source that gives the vertical difference between them—then I can plug those numbers into the formula and give you the slope gradient in degrees.  

Let me know the elevations (or the vertical difference), and I’ll do the calculation right away!
